subject.title: fix(memory): indexing survives transient embedding rate limits

question: Should retryAfterMs become an additive public ProviderHttpError plugin SDK contract, or should provider retry timing remain behind a narrower internal/provider-owned seam?
rationale: The extension boundary makes a typed shared seam reasonable, but publishing new ProviderHttpError metadata is a lasting external plugin API decision that cannot be inferred solely from this bug fix.

options.title: Approve Generic Metadata
options.body: Expose retryAfterMs as an additive ProviderHttpError field, document and test the contract, and let memory-core consume it through the SDK.

options.title: Keep Timing Provider-Local
options.body: Parse and propagate retry timing through a narrower provider-owned interface so ProviderHttpError does not gain a new public field.

options.title: Pause SDK Expansion
options.body: Land only the bounded indexing backoff after designing a separately reviewed generic retry-metadata contract.

recommendation.title: Approve Generic Metadata
recommendation.body: Expose retryAfterMs as an additive ProviderHttpError field, document and test the contract, and let memory-core consume it through the SDK.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available adjacent memory-core history owner for routing this cross-boundary decision, although direct ownership evidence is limited.
